clue.text: Enormous shade screening top of garden

indicators.note: a screen hides something behind it, so the shade word encloses the letter

parts.note: a shade is a hue, a tint of colour

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A huge sunshade keeps the top of a garden in shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' puts G, the first letter that 'top of' picks from 'garden', inside HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are plain synonyms for something of vast size.

clue.text: Brawl as drink stops sergeant major getting his cocktail

indicators.note: the drink plugs the gap like a stopper, sitting inside the abbreviation

parts.note: kir is a French drink of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of his are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out as drink interrupts the sergeant major's preparation of his cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir, a French aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur, is the drink; 'cocktail' looks like more drink but signals a mix of the letters of 'his'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a brief, small-scale fight, a synonym for a brawl.

clue.text: Friend held up favourite brown moth

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A friend lifts up a favourite brown moth to show it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns PAL into LAP, written upwards in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The lappet is a large brown European moth whose resting form looks like a dead leaf.

clue.text: One on court in engagement with Djokovic initially is set down

indicators.note: the one-on-court pair sits in the engagement word

parts.note: a date is an engagement or appointment
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word Djokovic

explanation.surface: A tennis player on court in a match with Djokovic has the schedule laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ICT inside DATE to give DICTATE, then 'initially' adds D from Djokovic.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to speak words for someone to write, so dictated words are set down on paper.

clue.text: Rich source of opals found in new mine close to Witwatersrand

indicators.note: new signals the letters are formed afresh in another order
the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

explanation.surface: Opals turn up in a fresh mine near the Witwatersrand, South Africa's gold-mining ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges O (from 'source of' opals) plus MINE into MONIE; 'close to' adds D, the last letter of Witwatersrand.
explanation.definitionFit: Monied, a variant of moneyed, describes people who have plenty of wealth.

clue.text: Get on all right in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: fair means all right or satisfactory, as in fair to middling

explanation.surface: Someone at an audition is asked whether they are getting on all right.
explanation.definitionFit: To fare is to manage or get on, as in 'how did you fare?'

clue.text: Fabric obtained from male sheep

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, rabbit or hare
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cloth woven from the wool of a male sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'male sheep' as one phrase; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen clothes.

clue.text: Mentally unbalanced setter joining most of staff in place to have a drink

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a bar is somewhere to have a drink
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: The setter, a bit unhinged, sits with some colleagues in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the insertion: 'joining' has to be read loosely as the setter and the short staff entering the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipolar disorder involves swings between mania and depression, a form of mental instability.

clue.text: Rush meal by river

parts.note: tea is an evening or afternoon meal in Britain
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone hurries their dinner down by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can mean an early evening meal as well as the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rush or dash, as in tearing down the road.

clue.text: Long to get hold of narrow piece of cloth

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
a strip is a narrow piece

explanation.surface: Someone longs to get their hands on a narrow scrap of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a cloth woven with very thin stripes, used for business suits.

clue.text: Disgusted by new American at university not standing!

parts.note: someone not standing is sitting down

explanation.surface: A newly arrived American at college is appalled to find no standing room!
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseated means sickened or repelled, a synonym for disgusted.

clue.text: Hard up family found in vacated squat

indicators.note: the family word is found inside the outer letters
a vacated word has been emptied of its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A poor family is discovered living in an abandoned squat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' leaves S and T of squat; 'found in' puts KIN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is British slang for having no money, the same as hard up.

clue.text: Share of extremely substantial diamonds

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone claims a portion of a large haul of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes S and L, the ends of 'substantial'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice is a portion or share, as in a slice of the profits.

clue.text: Prepared to look for a partner that's fashionable

parts.note: being up for something means being ready or prepared for it
to date is to go out with people seeking a romantic partner

explanation.surface: Someone ready to seek a partner who is stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to date means current or modern, a synonym for in fashion.

clue.text: Time spent making slight modification

parts.note: spent means exhausted, drained of strength

explanation.surface: Hours are spent making a small adjustment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' looks like a verb about passing time but is an adjective meaning worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small adjustment or fine-tuning change.

clue.text: Mine hard substance

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A mine yields a hard material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith means the essential core or substance of something, as in the pith of an argument.

clue.text: Be inclined to adopt summer's latest fashion

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in, so the letter is taken inside

parts.note: to tend is to be inclined to do something
the latest, or last, letter of summer is R

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to follow this summer's newest style.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a fashion or prevailing style of the moment.

clue.text: Couple stop as way to end a game of tennis

definitions.text: way to end a game of tennis

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join together
a break is a stop or pause

explanation.surface: A pair halt play to settle a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak is the extra game played to decide a tennis set level at six games all.

clue.text: Gang found in Cheshire town, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A gang has been spotted in a town in Cheshire, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, or informally a gang.

clue.text: Almost cool meal suitable for infants

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to chill is to cool
a dish is a course or meal

explanation.surface: A meal that has nearly cooled down is ready for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish means typical of or fit for young children.

clue.text: Ten dimes sent as deposit

indicators.note: sent in the sense of sent flying or scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten small coins are posted as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like money, matching the dimes, but here means settled matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit.

clue.text: Prisoner I meant to rescue

indicators.note: rescue is read as re-scue, the letters being saved and set out again in another order

explanation.surface: Someone protests they intended to free a jailed man.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person held in a prison or institution.

clue.text: Black stack of building material

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a rick is a stack of hay or straw

explanation.surface: A dark pile of construction supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks are fired clay blocks used to build walls.

clue.text: German car in which soundly to defeat the French

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word is taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: to beat is to defeat
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A German car in which to thrash the French team convincingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals the sound-alike BEET.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen Beetle is a classic small German car.

clue.text: University in conservative soap opera setting

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap opera

explanation.surface: A university sits amid a conservative soap opera's backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBRIDGE is the fictional village where The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap, is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is home to one of England's two ancient universities.

clue.text: Geological deposit found in Jurassic layer

indicators.note: the answer is found in the letters of the phrase, running across the word gap

explanation.surface: A deposit discovered in a rock stratum from the Jurassic period.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a fine-grained sedimentary material laid down in beds.

clue.text: Money for parties at hospital

parts.note: dos are parties, as in a big do

explanation.surface: Funds raised by holding parties at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for cash.

clue.text: Spain overcomes popular revolution

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over something means sitting above it

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for Spain
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Spain defeats a popular uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political upheaval but means a turning motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a rotation, one turning revolution.

clue.text: Bird eating a little green man?

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the bird word swallows the letter

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A bird gobbling up a tiny green figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors from Mars are popularly pictured as little green men; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Cathy's first to meet girl in charge of Wuthering Heights, say

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Cathy's

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Cathy meets a girl who runs Wuthering Heights, the house in Emily Brontë's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathy is the heroine of Wuthering Heights, so the surface treats it as a house rather than the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë's novel is an example of a great literary work of lasting standing.
